answers.answer: Starting cards: 2 players get 4 each, 3 players get 3 each, and 4 players get 2 each. Remove the Epidemic cards and set them aside before shuffling and dealing the remaining City and Event cards. Each player's pawn starts in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Remove Epidemic cards and set aside’; table gives 4/3/2 each; ‘Place matching colored pawns in Atlanta.’

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2. Flip 3 Infection cards and put 3 matching cubes in each named city; flip 3 more for 2 cubes each; flip 3 more for 1 cube each. Put all 9 revealed cards face up on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, ‘Infect initial cities’: leftmost ‘2’; 3 cards each at 3, 2, then 1 cube; nine cards face up in discard, remaining cards form deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove the unused Epidemic cards. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles as equally as possible, shuffle one Epidemic into each pile, then stack the piles with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, ‘Prepare the Player Deck’: 4/5/6 by difficulty, divide into equal-size-as-possible piles, one Epidemic in each, smaller piles on bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions, may repeat actions, and may stop early. Action-cost cards go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve Epidemics and reduce any over-limit hand, then infect cities; after all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: ‘up to 4’, may repeat or stop; action cards go to Player Discard Pile; phases are actions, draw 2, infect; play passes left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves to a city connected by a white line and has no card cost. Direct Flight discards the destination city's City card. Charter Flight discards the City card matching the city you are in and moves to any city. Shuttle Flight moves from a research-station city to any other research-station city. White lines crossing an edge wrap to the other edge, including Sydney–Los Angeles.
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules: ‘White lines going off one edge of the board wrap to the other edge (e.g., Sydney and Los Angeles are connected).’

answers.answer: Normally discard the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it there. If all 6 are built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than 6, set extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Build a Research Station action; Special Rules: ‘If more than 6 stations supplied: Set extras aside during setup.’

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one cured color in the city, but only 1 cube of one uncured color. Each additional color requires a separate action. Removed cubes return to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: ‘If that disease is cured, return all cubes of that one color’; ‘Treat each different color with a separate action’; cubes return to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 for the Scientist) and move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator; the station city's color need not match. Existing cubes remain and the disease may still infect until eradicated. If no cubes of that color are on the board, it is immediately eradicated and its marker is flipped.
answers.evidence: Discover a Cure and Cure Procedure: any research station, same-color cards, existing cubes remain; no cubes means immediately eradicate and flip marker.

answers.answer: Normally the transferable card is the City card matching the players' current city. Both players must be in that same city and agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card until within the limit.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge: give or take ‘the City card matching your current city’; ‘Both players must agree’; recipient exceeding 7 immediately discards or plays Event.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card, rather than only the matching-city card, to a player in the same city. This exception transfers from the Researcher's hand to the other player's hand and can happen on either player's turn. The other player cannot use this exception to give an arbitrary nonmatching card to the Researcher.
answers.evidence: Roles, Researcher: may give any City card to a player in same city; exception only transfers from Researcher's hand on either player's turn and does not allow arbitrary cards to Researcher.

answers.answer: After actions, draw the top 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the players lose; do not reshuffle discards.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: ‘Draw the top 2 cards together’; fewer than 2 means game ends and players lose, ‘do not reshuffle discards.’

answers.answer: First Increase: advance the Infection Rate marker one space. Then Infect: draw the bottom Infection card; because the city has 2 cubes of that color, add 1 to reach 3 and an outbreak occurs. Resolve the outbreak by advancing the Outbreaks marker and placing one cube of that color in each connected city (with any chain-reaction rules applying); discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify by reshuffling only that discard pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic from the game; do not draw a replacement Player card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards steps Increase, Infect (add only enough to reach 3, then outbreak; discard), Intensify; no replacement draw. Outbreaks section gives spread.

answers.answer: After 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics, flip 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards, respectively.
answers.evidence: Player Reference, Infection Rate Track: Epidemics 0–6 map to cards flipped 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

answers.answer: Resolve all three steps of the first Epidemic, then all three steps of the second; Events may be played between the two. When reducing an over-limit hand, first resolve any drawn Epidemics, then discard cards or play Events until at most 7.
answers.evidence: Epidemics: ‘resolve all 3 steps for the first, then all 3 steps for the second. Events may be played between the two’; Hand Limit says resolve Epidemics first.

answers.answer: Flip cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For a normal disease, place 1 matching cube; for an eradicated disease, place none; a cured but not eradicated disease can still receive cubes. If the city already has 3 of that color, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of deck, rate number, 1 cube, eradicated means none, 3 cubes causes outbreak; cured disease still infects until eradication; discard each card.

answers.answer: The first outbreak resolves by advancing the marker and spreading one cube to connected cities. A connected city already holding 3 cubes causes a chain-reaction outbreak after the current one resolves, advancing the marker again and spreading from that city. Do not add cubes to cities that already had an outbreak during resolution of this Infection card, so the spread does not add cubes back into the first city. The cap is 3 cubes per color per city; multiple colors can each have up to 3.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: chain reactions resolve after current outbreak; no cubes to cities that already had an outbreak during current card; cities may have multiple colors, up to 3 of each.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played after the Infection card is drawn but before resolving its outbreak, because Events cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card. After that card resolves, Airlift may be played before the next Infection card is drawn/resolved. The Event player chooses its use; it costs no action and is discarded to the Player Discard Pile. Airlift can move a pawn to any city; another player's pawn requires that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Events: may be played any time, but ‘Cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card’; Airlift effect; played Events go to Player Discard Pile. Events are not actions.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes 1 Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. Storage limit is 1 and it does not count against hand limit. When played, remove that Event from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Contingency Planner role: ‘As an action’, Event from ‘anywhere’ in Player Discard Pile, limit 1, doesn't count against hand limit; when played remove from game.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own; moving another player's pawn requires the owner's agreement. For Direct/Charter Flights, discards come from the Dispatcher's hand, and a Charter card matches the moved pawn's departure city. When directing another pawn, the Dispatcher may move it but cannot make it Treat Disease or perform other nonmovement actions. The Dispatcher cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Dispatcher role lists both options, owner's agreement, movement-only limitation, no Operations Expert move, and whose hand/city pays flight discards.

answers.answer: The players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; eradication and a clear board are not required. They lose if the Outbreaks marker reaches its last space (8th outbreak), if they cannot place required cubes of a needed color during an epidemic, outbreak, or infection, or if a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after actions.
answers.evidence: Victory: all 4 cures, diseases need not be eradicated; Defeat lists 8th outbreak, inability to place required cubes, and inability to draw 2 after actions.

answers.answer: Place the board within reach and put the 6 research stations and disease cubes nearby, separated by color; place 1 station in Atlanta; put the Outbreaks marker on 0 and the 4 cure markers vial-side up near the indicators. Give each player a Reference card, shuffle Role cards and deal 1 face up, place matching pawns in Atlanta, and remove unused Role cards and pawns. The player with the highest-population City card goes first.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 9 give supplies, marker placement, role/reference deal, pawn placement/removal, and first-player choice.

answers.answer: The active player decides what to do; teammates may offer advice. In Introductory games, play with cards face up for all to see. In Standard/Heroic games, hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may examine either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: active player decides; Special Rules: Introductory face up, Standard/Heroic private by default with experienced-group open-hand option, anyone may examine either discard pile.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube of an uncured disease has no effect and does not eradicate it. Removing the last cube of a cured disease eradicates it; flip its cure marker to the eradication side. Eradicated diseases receive no new cubes during normal infections or Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Eradication: last cube of cured disease flips marker; last cube of uncured disease has no effect; eradicated diseases get no new cubes during infections or epidemics.

answers.answer: Place 3 cubes in the city. There is no outbreak merely because the placement reaches 3; an outbreak occurs if the city already had 3 and the placement would require a fourth. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify reshuffles that pile onto the top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Infect: place 3 cubes unless eradicated; only if already holding cubes add enough to reach 3, then outbreak; discard to Infection Discard Pile, then Intensify.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. During Infect, draw the bottom Infection card, skip placing cubes because the disease is eradicated, and discard the card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify still reshuffles only that pile onto the top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic sequence; Infect draws bottom card and places 3 cubes ‘unless eradicated’, then discards the card; Intensify follows.

answers.answer: The first Epidemic's Intensify empties the Infection Discard Pile. The second Epidemic's bottom Infection card is then the only card in that pile when its Intensify occurs, so it is shuffled and placed on top of the deck. The next normal Infection draws that city first; since the Epidemic put 3 cubes there, it causes an outbreak (absent protection or other effects).
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics section: after first Intensify discard pile is empty; second bottom card is the only card shuffled, ends on top and is drawn first, normally causing outbreak.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 same-color City cards instead of 5 to Discover a Cure. The cure still must be discovered at any research station, and the cards must match the disease color; the station city's color need not match.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: 4 for Scientist at any research station; same-color cards; station city color need not match.

answers.answer: As an action, the Operations Expert builds a research station in the city they currently occupy. No City card is needed, used, or discarded.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert: ‘As an action: build a research station in the current city with no City card needed, used or discarded.’

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, the Operations Expert may move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The departure must be a city with a research station; the destination is any city; the card need not match either city.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert: ‘Once per turn as an action: move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.’

answers.answer: The Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one color from the current city, even when that disease is uncured. It cannot remove multiple colors with that single action.
answers.evidence: Medic: ‘Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color’; Treat Disease section treats each different color with a separate action.

answers.answer: When the cure is discovered while the Medic is already in the city, automatically remove all cubes of that cured color there immediately. Later, when another player moves the Medic into another city via Dispatcher or Airlift, the Medic automatically removes all cubes of that cured color there upon entering. These removals require no action by the Medic; the Dispatcher/Airlift movement is the other player's effect, with Airlift itself not an action.
answers.evidence: Medic role: already in city when cure discovered means remove cubes immediately; entering via Dispatcher or Airlift on another player's turn triggers automatic removal; cured disease cleanup has no action needed.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the Medic's city. This protection does not cover adjacent cities or uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Medic role: prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in Medic's city, but not adjacent cities or uncured diseases.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist prevents placements and outbreaks of every disease color in the Specialist's current city and all connected cities. The ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Quarantine Specialist role: every disease color in current and connected cities; setup cubes unaffected.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any one card from the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between an Epidemic's Infect and Intensify steps, so it can remove the Infection card just discarded during that Epidemic before Intensify reshuffles the pile.
answers.evidence: Event table: removes any 1 Infection Discard Pile card from game and may be played between Infect and Intensify.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, so no Infection cards are flipped for that step. It does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event table: ‘Skip the next Infect Cities step (do not flip Infection cards); does not skip an Epidemic’s Infect step.’

answers.answer: Airlift moves any one pawn to any city. If it is another player's pawn, get that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Event table, Airlift: ‘Move any 1 pawn to any city (get permission for another player's pawn).’

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the 7-card hand limit. Role cards and Reference cards do not count; an Event stored on the Contingency Planner Role card also does not count. For a hand of nine, first resolve any drawn Epidemics, then discard cards or play Event cards until at most 7.
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: Player cards only, max 7; Contingency Planner stored Event doesn't count; resolve Epidemics before reducing to 7.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, regardless of the player's location, with no City card discard needed.
answers.evidence: Event table, Government Grant: ‘Place a research station in any city (no card discard needed).’

answers.answer: Forecast lets the player draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 Infection cards, then put them back on top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Event table, Forecast: ‘Draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put them back on top.’
